### What are you really trying to do?

I want to be able to use any model through the [LitellmModel feature](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/models/litellm/) in the OpenAI Agents SDK on Temporal.

<!-- 
Tell us at a high level what you're doing, to avoid XY problem (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/XY_problem) 
-->

### Describe the bug

If you try specifying that your model is `LitellmModel(...)` instead of an OpenAI model string, you get the following error:
```
ValueError: Temporal workflows require a model name to be a string in the agent.
```

<!-- A clear and concise description of what the bug is. -->

<!-- If applicable, add screenshots or code blocks to help explain your problem. You can also use [Loom](http://loom.com/) to do short, free video bug reports. -->

### Minimal Reproduction

```
my_agent = Agent(
    name="my_agent",
    instructions="Say hello",
    model=LitellmModel(model="gemini/gemini-3-flash-preview", api_key=GEMINI_API_KEY),
)

@workflow.defn
class MyWorkflow:
    @workflow.run
    async def run(self, input: MyInput) -> str:
        result = await Runner.run(
            starting_agent= my_agent,
            input=input.prompt,
            max_turns=10,
        )
        return result.final_output_as(str)
```

comments.body: This is the intended behavior. LiteLLMModels _are_ usable, but you can't provide the model object at the workflow. This is because the model will need to be reconstructed in the model activities, where it won't have any configurations you put on in the workflow. For instance, even with this change, the `api_key` you provided to the model will not be present in the activity. The correct way to do this is to still use a string to choose the model, but customize your `model_provider`. See http://github.com/temporalio/samples-python/blob/main/openai_agents/model_providers/run_litellm_provider_worker.py

@tconley1428 [In this example](https://github.com/temporalio/samples-python/blob/main/openai_agents/model_providers/run_litellm_auto_workflow.py), it seems like the plugin should automatically detect that I am using a litellm model without specifying the `model_provider` -- is this still accurate? it doesn't seem to work.

but otherwise thanks for the heads up -- do you think it could ever be possible to support different providers in the `Agent` definition itself? i feel like that would be more intuitive, but if its too complex to implement, that's also understandable.
oops i realized that in that example -- i missed the worker being configured to use the provider in the other file

> but otherwise thanks for the heads up -- do you think it could ever be possible to support different providers in the Agent definition itself? i feel like that would be more intuitive, but if its too complex to implement, that's also understandable.

The problem I have with this is that while intuitive, it's not very robust. We could take the name from the model, but ensuring the provider matches that would involve some form of manual mapping, and a potential non-obvious loss of settings. The more robust way to do it would be to serialize the actual models in their entirety, but that is large and unlikely to be serializable.

Additionally:
> The plugin should automatically detect that I am using a litellm model

These are happening at different points. The provider configuration is when the worker is starting, while a different model could be selected dynamically at runtime. The provider would need to be an superset of all models you could potentially call, which doesn't really exist as a concept at the moment.

I'm not sure the example makes much sense in the SDK itself, but potentially it could be added as a sample to https://github.com/temporalio/samples-python/tree/main/openai_agents/model_providers which has a couple of other custom provider examples.
